segments.text: Think about a baby learning to walk. Does the baby fall? Yes, many times. Does the baby
say I'm a failure? No, the baby simply tries again. Falls, learns, gets up, and one day,
the baby walks. This is how all learning works. We learn, we make mistakes, we receive feedback,
we improve. Today, I want you to remember one simple sentence. There is no failure,
only feedback. Let's say it again. There is no failure, only feedback. Every mistake
teaches us something. Every challenge teaches us something. Every piece of feedback helps
us become better, but only if we are willing to learn.
One of the greatest basketball players of all time, Michael Jordan, once said, I've
missed more than 9,000 shots in my career. I've lost almost 300 games. I've failed over
and over and over again in my life, and that is why I succeed. Think about that. One of
the greatest athletes in history didn't become great because he never failed. He became great
because he learned from failure. Every missed shot became feedback. Every lost game became
feedback. Every mistake made him better. The same is true for us. Maybe today you make
a mistake at work. Maybe someone corrects you. Maybe your manager shows you a better
way. That does not mean you failed. It means you are learning. The question is not, did
I make a mistake? Because everyone makes mistakes. The real question is, what did I learn? Imagine
two people. The first person hears feedback and says, I already know. That's not my fault.
I've always done it this way. This person stops growing. Now look at the second person.
They say, thank you. Can you show me? How can I improve? This person grows every day.
The difference is not talent. The difference is attitude. Your relationship with feedback
will determine your growth. The people who grow the fastest usually receive the most
feedback. Not because they are worse, but because they are always learning. They ask questions.
They listen. They improve. Again, they ask questions. They listen. They improve.
There is another important lesson. If you want to improve, learn from people who are ahead
of you. Someone with more experience. Someone who has already solved the problem. Someone
who has already made the mistakes. Why? Because their experience becomes your shortcut. Instead
of learning everything the hard way, you can learn from their wisdom. But this requires
something important. Humility. Humility says, I don't know everything. I can still learn.
That attitude will take you much further than pretending you already know. People enjoy
working with someone who learns. Someone who accepts feedback. Someone who improves. Someone
who says, thank you. I'll do better next time. That kind of person becomes trusted. That kind
of person ends respect. That kind of person grows. So remember this. Mistakes are normal.
Learning is a choice. Feedback is a gift. Growth is a decision. Let's repeat that. Mistakes
are normal. Feedback is a gift. Growth is a decision. Mistake. Feedback. Learn. Improve. Repeat.
The next time you make a mistake, don't ask am I a failure. Instead ask, what is this teaching me?
What can I do better next time? What feedback can I learn from? Because there is no failure.
Only feedback. And every piece of feedback is another opportunity to become a better worker,
a better teammate, and a better person.
